slides.title: Zava's Local AI Developer Stack
slides.subtitle: Surface Laptop Ultra with NVIDIA RTX Spark
slides.takeaway: Protect engineering IP locally; keep an approved cloud lane for heavier reasoning.
slides.notes: Zava's source code and CAD/PLM data are sensitive IP. This proposal keeps frequent coding and internal-document work local while reserving a controlled cloud path for the heaviest reasoning. We will inspect the stack, distinguish memory views, examine measured throughput and agree a technical pilot. The goal is evidence, not a device-wide performance promise.

layers.label: Surface Laptop Ultra
layers.detail: RTX Spark N1X; Blackwell RTX GPU; 20 CPU cores

slides.notes: Surface Laptop Ultra uses NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X, a Blackwell RTX GPU, and 20 CPU cores. The installed runtimes are llama.cpp build 11573, native ARM64 with CUDA, and Foundry Local with its CUDA execution provider. They are alternative serving paths, not serial stages. The local catalog contains 28 open models occupying 315 GiB.

slides.title: Memory Views Are Not Additive
slides.takeaway: Installed memory, Windows visibility and GPU budgeting describe distinct views, not separate pools.
slides.notes: These are distinct views of memory on the same device. The installed capacity is 128 GB; about 64 GB is visible to Windows; nvidia-smi reports a 64,000 MiB GPU budget. Never add them together or label system RAM dedicated VRAM. Validate model fit alongside context and workload memory during the pilot.

slides.title: Measured Decode On This Device
slides.takeaway: These shared-machine measurements guide testing, not guaranteed production throughput.

data.caption: Approximate decode; Local-AI-Bench, October 2026; shared machine

slides.notes: Local-AI-Bench measured approximate single-stream decode on this device in October 2026: Qwen3-Coder 30B at 86 tokens/s, Gemma 4 26B at 72, and dense Qwen3.6 27B at 13. The machine was shared. These are observations, not guaranteed specifications or comparisons with other devices. Decode throughput does not establish task accuracy or total interaction latency.

slides.title: Concurrency Changes Aggregate Throughput
slides.takeaway: Aggregate tokens describe shared serving capacity, not each developer's response speed.
slides.notes: Qwen3-Coder 30B reached about 140 tokens/s across 4 concurrent streams. Gemma 4 26B reached about 245 tokens/s across 8. These aggregate results do not describe per-request speed or equal-load comparisons. Qwen3-Coder's measured first-token latency was 0.13 seconds. Source: Local-AI-Bench, this device, October 2026, shared machine; not guaranteed specifications.

slides.title: MoE Works Like A Specialist Workshop
slides.takeaway: MoE selects specialists per token; dense models engage broader computation.
slides.notes: Qwen3-Coder 30B is MoE, with about 3B active parameters per token. Its Q4_K_M file is 17.3 GiB. Selecting specialists reduces active computation; it does not shrink the stored model to the active parameter count. Dense Qwen3.6 27B engages broader computation each token. The measured decode difference is not evidence of greater accuracy.

slides.title: Model Bands Guide Fit, Not Accuracy
slides.takeaway: Choose parameter bands for planning, then measure quality on representative Zava tasks.
slides.notes: S spans 1–4B parameters, M 7–8B, L 14–20B and XL 24–32B. These are planning estimates, not accuracy tiers. Start with representative code and document tasks, then assess model fit alongside context, latency and acceptance rate. A larger parameter count does not demonstrate higher quality.

slides.title: RAG Is Your Engineering Librarian
slides.takeaway: RAG brings relevant internal passages into a local model's answer context.
slides.notes: Proposed pilot RAG: ingest approved engineering documents, chunk and embed locally, retrieve relevant passages, and supply them as context to local generation. The librarian analogy separates retrieval from model knowledge. Retain source links so engineers can inspect evidence. Retrieval can miss relevant passages, and generated answers require review. Keep CAD/PLM data within approved local access boundaries.

slides.title: Local By Default, Cloud By Policy
slides.takeaway: Keep sensitive work local; approve non-sensitive payloads before cloud reasoning.
slides.notes: Proposed pilot architecture: developer requests enter a policy router. Code and internal-document work stay local; approved documents feed local embeddings and retrieval. Retrieved passages ground local inference through either runtime. Only approved, non-sensitive heavy-reasoning payloads may leave for cloud models. Deny uncertain outbound requests; enforce document permissions and inspect egress. These controls are design requirements, not claimed certifications.

slides.title: Validate The Developer Loop
slides.takeaway: Treat generation as a reviewed draft, then measure the developer experience.

slides.notes: Pilot representative, permissioned tasks: code generation, code explanation and internal-document questions. Retrieve context when useful, not automatically for every request. Engineers review changes and source evidence, then run existing tests. Capture acceptance rate, latency and developer experience. Agree acceptance criteria before starting; do not treat throughput as a productivity measurement.

slides.title: Approve Zava's Local AI Pilot
slides.takeaway: Start with 10 developers for 2 weeks; expand only on measured evidence.

steps.label: Select pilot team
steps.detail: 10 developers covering coding and document retrieval

steps.label: Run real tasks
steps.detail: 2 weeks using approved code and engineering documents

steps.label: Review evidence
steps.detail: Acceptance rate, latency and developer experience

slides.notes: Choose a pilot owner and representative developers, define approved data boundaries and agree acceptance criteria before starting. Run local code generation and internal-document RAG, with policy-approved cloud routing for eligible heavy reasoning. After 2 weeks, review acceptance rate, latency and developer experience together. Decide next steps from evidence, not peak throughput.
